trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation; 48 hours for the 3 enterprise customers whose contracts say so
notify: Each affected customer's security contact (then the customer administrator)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, all customers. Plan to the 48-hour clock

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer, involving personal information of Florida residents as defined in 501.171(1)(g) (on this platform, mainly a user name or email address with a password that would permit access to an online account)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. Give the customer all information it needs for its own notices
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), which then gives notice under 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida personal information is involved (about 18,000 Florida workers). Counsel decides whether salted, hashed passwords are 'secured' and therefore excluded (501.171(1)(g)2.)

obligation: California service provider notice to the data owner
trigger: The company maintains computerized data it does not own, and California residents' personal information (as defined in 1798.82(h)) was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person
notify: Owner or licensee of the data (each affected customer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if California personal information was acquired (about 9,500 California workers). Worked example of a service-provider duty in another state

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected workers reside (46 states). For customer worker data the customers own the data and usually give resident notices; the company supports them under the DPA. Counsel checks each state's definition of personal information against the data elements taken

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-owned data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company owns (for example, customer administrator sign-in credentials or its own employees' data) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. Not required if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines in writing that identity theft or other financial harm is not likely; keep that determination 5 years and send it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(4)(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Only for data the company owns, not customer worker data

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, where the company is the covered entity
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (15 more days for notice to individuals, not this notice, if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity (company-owned data) and 500 or more Florida individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity and more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment (including a data-theft extortion demand)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. POL-03 4.7 also requires Chief Executive Officer, counsel, and insurer approval

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. The company is under the SBA size standard; recheck the sector-based criteria when the rule is final

trigger: Breach of CPNI held by a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination; customers only after 7 full business days post-LE notice (unless urgent/LE directs otherwise)
notify: USSS and FBI via FCC central reporting facility; then customers
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a carrier or VoIP provider and holds no CPNI

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: Bank service provider notification (IT/data processors serving banks)
trigger: Incident that materially disrupts or degrades covered services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible when an incident materially disrupts/degrades covered services for 4+ hours
notify: Bank-designated point of contact at each affected banking organization customer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no banking organization customers today. Recheck if a bank signs up

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
